entries.name: Silicon MOS spin qubits
entries.summary: Electron spins in gate-defined quantum dots at a Si/SiO2 interface, fabricated with industrial 300 mm CMOS processes. The thesis: if qubit structures survive full foundry rules, the semiconductor industry's uniformity, yield and scale become available to quantum processors.
entries.scaling_hypothesis: Foundry-fabricated 2D-scalable qubit arrays plus co-integrated cryo-CMOS control reach utility scale without bespoke quantum fabs.
falsifiers: Si/SiO2 interface charge noise or valley-splitting variability cannot sustain >99% two-qubit gates at array scale under foundry tolerances
Per-qubit wiring/measurement overhead defeats co-integration before the error-corrected regime is reached
Yield of quantum-dot devices across a full 300 mm wafer stays too low for tiled processors

entries.name: Fusion-based photonic quantum computing
entries.summary: Photonic qubits in silicon-photonics chips, entangled into a lattice through two-qubit fusion measurements; utility scale requires millions of near-identical photonic components manufactured in a high-volume fab.
entries.scaling_hypothesis: All hard physics lives in components that a telecom-grade fab can mass-produce; scale becomes a manufacturing and integration problem rather than a coherence problem.
falsifiers: End-to-end photon loss (source → switching → detection) cannot be pushed below the fusion-tolerance threshold at system scale
Optical switching speed or detector efficiency does not reach the fusion network's simultaneous requirements
Cryogenic loading of millions of detectors makes the refrigeration plant impractical

entries.name: Trapped-ion (QCCD) processors
entries.summary: Ions held and shuttled in RF traps; state-of-the-art fidelities with slow gates and wiring/packaging pressure as zones multiply.
entries.scaling_hypothesis: QCCD shuttling and modular photonic networking scale a high-fidelity core into a larger system.
falsifiers: Gate throughput and shuttling overhead keep useful circuit depth below utility requirements at achievable clock rates

entries.name: Modular superconducting processors
entries.summary: Transmon-class superconducting qubits tiled into modular processors; mature fab and control ecosystem with coherence and crosstalk limits.
entries.scaling_hypothesis: Modular interconnection of proven processor units plus steady fidelity gains reaches fault tolerance incrementally.
falsifiers: Interconnect loss between modules prevents the modular step from counting as scaling

entries.name: Neutral-atom arrays
entries.summary: Optically trapped atom arrays with Rydberg-mediated gates; naturally large qubit counts with mid-circuit reload and fidelity questions.
entries.scaling_hypothesis: Optical addressing scales atom counts faster than electrode wiring scales other modalities.
falsifiers: Atom loss and reload overhead dominate as array size grows toward error-corrected operation

entries.name: Bosonic superconducting qubits
entries.summary: Error-resilient bosonic encodings in superconducting resonators, trading qubit count for per-qubit protection.
entries.scaling_hypothesis: Hardware-level error suppression reduces the QEC overhead enough that fewer physical modes reach utility.
falsifiers: Residual error channels do not suppress far enough to offset the added hardware complexity

entries.name: Precision atom qubits in silicon
entries.summary: Single dopant atoms placed with atomic precision in isotopically pure silicon; STM-defined fabrication.
entries.scaling_hypothesis: Atomic-precision placement produces perfectly identical qubits, trading throughput for uniformity.
falsifiers: STM-based fabrication throughput cannot populate utility-scale arrays

entries.name: Optically linked silicon spin qubits
entries.summary: Silicon spin qubits entangled through photonic links, combining spin-qubit density with optical networking.
entries.scaling_hypothesis: Optical interconnect removes the wiring wall that limits monolithic spin arrays.
falsifiers: Spin-photon interface efficiency never reaches the entanglement rate the architecture assumes

entries.name: Topological superconducting qubits
entries.summary: Majorana-based topological qubits aiming for hardware-level error protection; the qubit's existence and controllability remain the open question.
entries.scaling_hypothesis: Topological protection collapses QEC overhead by orders of magnitude if the base qubit works.
falsifiers: The underlying topological excitation cannot be demonstrated with the braiding fidelity the architecture requires

entries.name: Photonic testbed-class platforms
entries.summary: Photonic systems built for algorithm demonstration rather than the fusion-lattice utility-scale path — e.g. NQCC's Aegiq and ORCA testbeds.
entries.scaling_hypothesis: Near-term photonic systems test application mapping while utility-scale photonics is built elsewhere.
falsifiers: Photon losses cap problem size below anything application-relevant
